issues.legal_issue: Concurrent findings that premises are bona fide required for the landlord’s personal use are not disturbed in a special-leave appeal absent perversity or misinterpretation or misapplication of law.
material_facts: The eviction suit was based on the landlord’s bona fide need to provide business premises for her sons.
The sons lacked suitable business accommodation: one operated a tailoring business in a small passage, another had no shop for his repair business, and a third intended to start a laundry business.
The trial court, the appellate court, and the High Court all found the requirement genuine and bona fide.
The tenant did not establish that the concurrent finding was perverse or that relevant law had been misinterpreted or misapplied.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to disturb the concurrent finding of bona fide requirement.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal by special leave, a concurrent finding of fact is not to be overturned unless it is shown to be perverse or the relevant law has been misinterpreted or misapplied. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.special_leave_eviction_appeal: A tenant pursued a special-leave appeal against an eviction decree.
predicates.concurrent_bona_fide_need_findings: The courts below consistently found that the landlord genuinely required the premises for personal use.
predicates.no_perversity_or_legal_error_shown: The appellant did not show that the concurrent finding was perverse or resulted from misinterpretation or misapplication of law.

issues.definition: When a tenant brings a special-leave eviction appeal, the courts below have consistently found a genuine personal need, and no perversity or legal error is shown, the finding is not disturbed.

issues.legal_issue: Requirements governing eviction for reconstruction do not invalidate an eviction decree founded on bona fide personal need when reconstruction was not the basis of the suit and the tenant’s asserted reconstruction requirements were found satisfied in any event.
material_facts: The eviction suit was brought on the ground of the landlord’s bona fide personal requirement, not on a reconstruction ground.
The tenant did not raise the reconstruction-ground plea in the trial court and acknowledged before the appellate court that the suit was not based on that ground.
The appellate court found that the relevant plans and estimates had been prepared and that the landlord had the necessary resources for the proposed changes.
The tenant nevertheless argued on appeal that the decree should fail for non-compliance with the requirements governing reconstruction.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not succeed on the reconstruction argument because the suit was not based on reconstruction; in any event, the appellate court had found the relevant requirements satisfied.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(1)(h) of the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961, concerns eviction for building, rebuilding, or substantial alterations, and subsection (7) prescribes conditions for an eviction order on that ground. Those conditions did not defeat this suit, which was based on bona fide personal need under Section 12(1)(f); additionally, the appellate court found the relevant requirements satisfied. The Supreme Court did not rely on an earlier case for this holding.

predicates.tenant_eviction_appeal: A tenant appealed an eviction decree.
predicates.suit_based_on_personal_need: The landlord brought the suit on the ground of bona fide personal need rather than to carry out reconstruction.
predicates.tenant_disclaimed_reconstruction_ground_: The tenant accepted in the lower appellate court that the suit was not based on a reconstruction ground.
predicates.reconstruction_requirements_found_satisf: The lower appellate court found that the relevant plans, estimates, and resources for the proposed work were in place.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals an eviction decree based on personal need, had accepted below that the suit was not based on reconstruction, and the lower appellate court found the relevant reconstruction requirements satisfied, a reconstruction-based challenge is rejected.
